lines_of_business: Medicare Advantage Plans (criteria apply only to CPT 37500, 37785, S2202; all other codes follow CMS NCD/LCD)
effective_or_revised: Effective 05|01|2019; Policy last updated 07|07|2021 (library metadata says 2021 posting)
sections_in_order: Medical Criteria (Medicare Advantage Plans; Commercial Products)
Background (saphenous veins, types of treatment, perforators, MOCA, FDA devices)
criteria_location: Medical Criteria, pp.1-3, written twice (Medicare Advantage block and Commercial block with minor differences). Policy Statement p.3 adds exclusions (MOCA, telangiectasia, concurrent perforator). Coding pp.7-8 adds not-medically-necessary code lists. Background is narrative only.
procedures_covered: Ligation and stripping by RF/thermal ablation or EVLT
Transilluminated powered phlebectomy and ambulatory phlebectomy
SEPS / RF / laser / Linton perforator ligation

logic.top_level: all: a general treatment gate (duplex + 6 weeks conservative + one of six indications) AND a method-specific criterion

k_of_n.quote: meets one of the listed criteria below: stasis ulcer of the lower leg, significant pain and significant edema that interferes with activities of daily living, bleeding ..., recurrent episodes of superficial phlebitis, stasis dermatitis, or refractory dependent edema

logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: Policy Statement sentences: MOCA 'not medically necessary'; telangiectasia sclerotherapy 'contract exclusion'; concurrent perforator ligation not medically necessary. No contraindication list.
logic.initial_vs_repeat: Only a utilization note on sclerotherapy: 'Requests for greater than 3 sclerotherapy sessions in a 12-month period will be reviewed to determine the need for additional treatment'. That is a review trigger, not a denial rule.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: significant pain and significant edema that interferes with activities of daily living
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Pain AND edema are both required in that item, unlike the other five single-finding items; 'that interferes' attaches to edema grammatically.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: The greater saphenous and/or lesser saphenous and/or accessory saphenous vein is competent; removed, ablated, or EVLT/RFA/EVLA is planned.
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: 'and/or' stacks; the semicolon splits competent / removed / ablated / planned in a way that mixes patient state with a plan; read as any-of.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: The greater saphenous and/or lesser saphenous and/or accessory saphenous vein is competent; or removed or ablated.
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Echosclerotherapy says 'and/or' for which vein, so one competent vein or all?

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Ligation and Stripping by either Radiofrequency/Thermal ablation (RFA/EVLA) or endovenous laser therapy (EVLT®)
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: One heading covers ligation and stripping (surgery) and endovenous ablation; the only criterion is that the saphenous vein is incompetent.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: chronic venous insufficiency (greater, lesser, or accessory saphenous and symptomatic varicose tributaries) has been eliminated
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Reads that CVI itself is eliminated; meant that the superficial veins listed have been eliminated.

requirement_kinds.quote: if the member has had a duplex ultrasound
remains symptomatic after 6 weeks of conservative therapy*
The components of the conservative therapy include, but are not limited to: weight reduction, a daily exercise plan, periodic leg elevation, and use of graduated stockings
Conservative therapy must be documented in the medical record. Inability to tolerate compressive bandages or stockings and the reason for such intolerance must be documented
stasis ulcer of the lower leg ... bleeding associated with the diseased vessels ... recurrent episodes of superficial phlebitis, stasis dermatitis, or refractory dependent edema
significant pain and significant edema that interferes with activities of daily living
The veins must be >2 mm and <6 mm
The perforator veins greater than 3.5 mm in size
chronic venous insufficiency (greater, lesser, or accessory saphenous and symptomatic varicose tributaries) has been eliminated
Leg ulcers have not resolved following combined superficial vein treatment and compression therapy for at least 3 months
The venous insufficiency is not secondary to deep venous thromboembolism.

codes.codes_tied_to_criteria: Partly. Medicare Advantage criteria apply only to 37500, 37785 and S2202; commercial lists many CPT codes as 'medically necessary when the medical criteria above are met' but the method criteria are by modality name, not by code, and sclerotherapy and phlebectomy codes are not mapped to a block. 37500 is a deleted code (deleted 2026 per BCBSFL) but is still in this 2021 policy.
codes.non_covered_code_lists: 36468 not covered (cosmetic); 36473 not medically necessary (commercial); Medicare Advantage list includes 36473 as medically necessary via online tool.

external_dependencies.what: Medicare Advantage: all codes other than 37500/37785/S2202 follow CMS NCD/LCD via the online authorization tool
external_dependencies.quote: For all other codes, Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Rhode Island (BCBSRI) follows the medical necessity criteria from Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) National and Local Coverage Determinations (NCD/LCD).

external_dependencies.what: Prior authorization via web tool, criteria not in this document
external_dependencies.quote: Prior Authorization via Web-Based Tool for Procedures

definitions_that_change_meaning.definition_quote: include, but are not limited to: weight reduction, a daily exercise plan, periodic leg elevation, and use of graduated stockings
ranging from class 0 (no visible sign of disease) to class 6 (active ulceration)

vague_terms.quote: remains symptomatic after 6 weeks of conservative therapy
vague_terms.problem: Does 'conservative therapy' require all four components or any? 'include, but are not limited to'.

vague_terms.quote: will be reviewed to determine the need for additional treatment
vague_terms.problem: Soft limit, not a rule; no standard given.

vague_terms.quote: when the medical criteria is met for both treatment and the method
vague_terms.problem: Two-layer rule stated only in Policy Statement; a parser reading the Medical Criteria section might miss that both layers are required.

extraction_hazards: Medical Criteria appear twice (Medicare Advantage and Commercial) with different content (commercial adds Sclerotherapy 2-6 mm and phlebectomy; MA omits them) and inconsistent indentation; text order interleaves page footers ('500 EXCHANGE STREET ... MEDICAL COVERAGE POLICY | 1').
Page break splits the method list: the heading 'Ligation and Stripping ...' is at the bottom of page 1 and its only bullet at the top of page 2.
Bullets with hanging footnote asterisks; the footnote text sits between list and next paragraph.
Echosclerotherapy and Sclerotherapy bullets look like one list; thresholds (>2 mm and <6 mm vs >3.5 mm) are easily misattached.

Background paragraph about FDA devices is truncated mid-sentence ('treatment of incompetent great saphenous veins, accessory saphenous veins and visible varicosities of the great') and a heading 'PUBLISHED' / 'Determinations' at the end are residue from the web page.
Coding lists use different descriptor wording from AMA (e.g. 'sclerosing solution'), and a '*only the primary procedure needs preauthorization' footnote floats under 37780.
interesting_structures: Two-layer rule: general treatment gate plus a method-specific gate, stated as 'both treatment and the method' in the Policy Statement.
Duplicated criteria blocks by line of business with the Medicare Advantage block scoped by CPT code list.
Delegation by code: for most MA codes the document says 'follow CMS' and has no criteria at all.
Prior auth required for MA, merely 'recommended' for commercial.
Session-count review trigger (>3 per 12 months) rather than a hard cap.

fit_to_tree.scale: 1 = all/any/not expresses it cleanly ... 5 = needs new constructs or human judgment
fit_to_tree.why: The shape is an all-of with a 1-of-6 list and a per-method leaf, which a tree handles. Strain comes from two lines of business in one file, duplicated and slightly different blocks, delegation to CMS for most codes, and method criteria that depend on whether other veins are competent/removed/planned (state plus plan).
